thread:
aj_parker: Ran side-by-side replay vs synthetic (30m) on staging. Noticed p95 TTFT regressed ~12% when kernel selection flipped during a burst.

maria_g: ouch. kernel flip as in runtime decided to swap attn kernel? any KV hit rate changes?

aj_parker: yep runtime log shows kernel selector switching attn_v2 -> attn_compat at ~10:12:04, coincident with an autoscaler pod handoff. KV cache warm hit dropped from ~84% -> 62% for ~18s.

sasha_choi: do we have the exact lines? can you paste a small tail of the profiling output?

aj_parker: pasted snippet from profiler + runtime logs: 
```
[10:12:02] kernel_select: chosen=attn_v2 score=0.82
[10:12:04] kernel_swap: from=attn_v2 to=attn_compat reason=mem_fragmentation
[10:12:05] kvcache: hit_rate=0.62 (was 0.84)
[10:12:05] ttft_p95=138ms (baseline 123ms)
```

ben_h: interesting. That lines up with the autoscaler moving a batch to a different GPU that has a different kernel build. Could be kernel binary choice + cold KV segments.

maria_g: was this seen in synthetic? iirc synthetic harness uses uniform sequence lengths and always pins kernel.

aj_parker: correct — synthetic run stayed pinned to attn_v2 and had stable KV hits and p95. The replay run triggers kernel churn because of multi-model request shapes and runtime heuristics.

replay-bot: summary uploaded: https://harness/replays/1971234567/summary (contains waterfall, p95 timeline, kernel-switch markers)

sasha_choi: so two hypotheses: 1) kernel swap causes a short-term perf penalty because attn_compat has slower per-token latency, and 2) KV cache locality lost during pod handoff reduces goodput for short window. both would push TTFT/p95 up.

ben_h: agree. also remember TTFT measures time-to-first-token (includes kernel init path and KV lookup). TPOT would be less impacted if goodput (tokens/sec) after first token recovers. we should look at TPOT and goodput vs QPS curves.

maria_g: next steps I'd run a controlled canary: replay harness with deterministic seed, force kernel pinning off/on, and toggle "preserve-kvcache-on-handoff" flag. collect pprof on both kernels and NVTX to see GPU stall reasons.

aj_parker: plan: (1) replay 10x with kernel_pin=true (2) replay 10x kernel_pin=false (3) synthetic with same traffic shape but with random pod handoff injection. compare metrics: TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT p50/p95, goodput (tokens/sec), qps. I'll attach runs to the issue.

sasha_choi: add microtrace: measure kvcache lookup latency distribution (ms buckets) and kernel dispatch time. Create a small metric dashboard tile: kvcache_hit_rate, kernel_swap_count, ttft_p95.

ben_h: also log device model + kernel binary hash on each request so we can ensure apples-to-apples when comparing.

aj_parker: noted. I'll add those tags and run. If we still see regression with pinned kernels then it's likely KV cold behavior. If only when kernel_swap happens then focus on kernel selection logic.

maria_g: thanks. tagging perf/regressions and runtime oncall. :thumbsup:

sasha_choi: ping me once you have the pprof flamegraphs, I can diff them for memory traffic patterns.

aj_parker: will do. saving run ids to the thread. Thanks all.
